articles.title: Revolut confirms customer data breach through fake government requests | TechCrunch
articles.text:
British fintech Revolut confirmed that it disclosed sensitive customer information to an unauthorized third party after receiving fraudulent requests sent from a legitimate government agency email domain.
The exposed data included customers’ identity and contact details, including their birth date, postal and email addresses, and phone numbers, as well as copies of their identity documents including passports and driver’s licenses, according to a notification emailed to affected customers and reviewed by TechCrunch. The data may have also included verification selfies, account statements, and transaction histories, the firm said in its notification.
A Revolut spokesperson confirmed to TechCrunch that a “limited” number of customers were impacted and said the company had contacted those customers directly. Revolut, however, did not disclose the exact number of impacted individuals. It also did not answer whether the incident was limited to a specific market and declined to disclose the government agency involved.
“Revolut recently identified a sophisticated external impersonation scam where an unauthorised third party utilised a legitimate government agency domain email to submit fraudulent requests for information,” the spokesperson said.
Revolut told TechCrunch that it blocked the email address after discovering the scam from the unauthorized third party and alerted the relevant government agency, law enforcement, and relevant regulators, adding, “Revolut systems and customer funds are unaffected.”
London-based Revolut has more than 80 million customers globally and operates as a bank in more than 30 countries, per its website. The fintech recently expanded its presence in markets including India, Mexico, France, and the UAE. Moreover, earlier this month, the U.S. Office of the Comptroller of the Currency granted a conditional approval to Revolut to set up a national bank in the country, which the firm expects to launch in the first half of 2027.
Well-known crypto security researcher ZachXBT posted about Revolut’s email to its affected customers late on Friday. The researcher said the incident appeared to have been targeted at high net worth users.
The incident comes as Revolut reportedly weighs a potential public listing that could value it at as much as $200 billion, up from its $75 billion private valuation in November. The fintech has also been expanding its banking footprint in Europe and globally, securing banking licenses in France and the UK in recent months.

articles.title: 0,85 mm dünn: Diese hocheffiziente Solarfolie klebt auf jeder Oberfläche
articles.text:
Nur 0,85 Millimeter dünn: Diese hocheffiziente Solarfolie klebt auf jeder Oberfläche
Flexible Solarfolien sind nichts Neues. Aufgebracht auf E-Autos sollen sie deren Reichweite verlängern. Zudem sollen sie in transparenter Ausführung auf Fensterscheiben geklebt werden können und so zusätzliche Energie für private Haushalte liefern.
Solarwindow startet Verkauf von Solarfolie
Das US-Unternehmen Solarwindow Technologies hat jetzt den Verkaufsstart einer Solarfolie angekündigt, die nicht nur ultradünn und flexibel ist, sondern auch mit einem hohen Wirkungsgrad punkten kann. Einem Bericht von pv-magazine.com zufolge soll die Zelleffizienz der nur 0,85 Millimeter dicken Solarfolie 24,4 Prozent erreichen und sich damit auf dem Niveau moderner Solarmodule bewegen.
Die selbstklebende Folie eignet sich vor allem für flache und gebogene Oberflächen sowie für Anwendungen, bei denen es auf jedes Gramm ankommt und wo herkömmliche Module nicht geeignet sind. Mit Electrolux zielt Solarwindow eigenen Angaben zufolge auf die Bereiche Transportwesen, Luft- und Raumfahrt, Landwirtschaft, Infrastruktur sowie Gebäudearchitektur ab.
Electroflex: Marktstart in den USA
Zunächst liefert Solarwindow die Folie nur an industrielle Hersteller in den USA aus. In den kommenden Quartalen sollen weitere Märkte in Nordamerika und Asien dazukommen. Ob irgendwann auch private Haushalte oder kleinere Firmen die Solarfolie kaufen können, ist nicht bekannt.
Bisher hatte sich Solarwindow auf die Entwicklung einer transparenten, flüssigen Beschichtung für Glas- und Kunststoffoberflächen konzentriert. Liquidelectricity soll auch in Innenräumen und bei schattigen Verhältnissen Strom erzeugen können.
Strategiewechsel euphorisiert die Börse
Mit Electroflex erweitert Solarwindow sein Portfolio jetzt um physische, flexible Solarprodukte. Das Ganze ist Teil eines Mitte August 2026 kommunizierten Strategiewechsels hin zu einer breiter aufgestellten Energieplattform. Neben Electroflex und Liquidelectricity sollen weitere neue Produkte kommen, wie Solarwindow-CEO Amit Singh ankündigte.
An der Börse hatte das für Euphorie gesorgt, wie es bei boerse-express.com heißt. Innerhalb der vergangenen zwei Wochen hatte sich der Kurs der Aktie des Unternehmens mehr als versiebenfacht. Ob die Hochstimmung anhält, hängt laut Beobachter:innen aber davon ab, ob die angekündigten detaillierten Produktinformationen sowie die Updates zur Produktzertifizierung halten, was sie versprechen.
Dieser Artikel wurde ursprünglich am 31.08.2026 veröffentlicht, interessiert jedoch immer noch sehr viele unserer Leser:innen. Deshalb haben wir ihn aktualisiert und hier nochmals zur Verfügung gestellt.

articles.title: How Professional Computer Repair Can Help Australian Businesses Reduce Downtime and Stay Productive - Tech Guide
articles.text:
For most Australian businesses, computers are no longer simply office equipment. They are part of the infrastructure that keeps everyday operations moving.
Employees use them to communicate with customers, prepare documents, access financial systems, manage projects, store important information and work with cloud-based applications. When those systems perform reliably, business can continue without much interruption. When they begin to fail, even a relatively small technical problem can quickly turn into lost time and unnecessary disruption.
Professional Computer Repair can play an important role in helping businesses deal with these problems before they develop into larger disruptions. A computer that repeatedly freezes, takes too long to start or struggles with everyday software might not appear to be a serious business concern at first. Yet when several employees experience similar problems, the effect can become much larger. Work gets delayed, staff have to find temporary solutions and business owners may end up spending valuable time dealing with technology instead of focusing on customers and growth.
The right approach is not simply to fix a machine after it stops working. Businesses also need to understand why problems occur, whether existing equipment remains suitable for its workload and how individual computers fit into the wider IT environment. This broader perspective can help companies maintain more dependable systems while making better decisions about repairs, upgrades, replacements and ongoing support.
Why Small Technology Problems Can Have a Big Business Impact
Technology problems rarely arrive at a convenient time. A computer may suddenly stop working before an important presentation, a storage drive may begin showing signs of failure while an employee is working on a critical project, or a network issue may prevent several people from accessing files and applications.
The direct cost of such an incident is only part of the problem. Employees may be unable to complete their normal responsibilities while the issue is being investigated. Customers may experience delays, appointments can be affected and important internal tasks may be pushed further behind schedule.
This is why businesses should look beyond the question of whether a computer is technically operational. A machine can still turn on while performing poorly enough to affect productivity. Slow storage, insufficient memory, outdated software, overheating and hardware degradation can all reduce the efficiency of an otherwise functional computer.
Identifying these issues early allows businesses to decide whether a device needs maintenance, an upgrade or replacement. In some cases, a relatively straightforward repair may restore a computer to a useful working condition. In others, continued repairs may no longer make financial sense.
Business Computer Work Requires More Than Basic Troubleshooting
The technology requirements of a business are different from those of a typical home user. A business computer may need to connect to shared files, printers, servers, cloud applications, security systems and other workplace devices. Changing one part of that setup without considering the rest can create additional problems.
This is where professional business computer work becomes valuable. Rather than treating each machine as an isolated device, technicians can consider how computers fit into the wider workplace environment.
For example, setting up a new workstation may involve installing required applications, transferring data, configuring email, connecting printers and ensuring the device can access appropriate shared resources. Upgrading an existing computer may also require checking compatibility with current software and network systems.
A structured approach can help businesses maintain more consistent technology across their workplace. It also makes it easier to identify older equipment, plan future upgrades and avoid situations where employees are using significantly different systems for similar tasks.
Preventive Maintenance Can Be Better Than Emergency Repairs
Many businesses only think about IT support after something stops working. While reactive support is important, preventing recurring problems can be even more valuable.
Regular maintenance can reveal warning signs before they develop into complete failures. Storage health, system performance, software updates, backups and security settings can all be reviewed as part of a wider technology maintenance strategy.
This does not mean every business needs an expensive technology overhaul. Often, relatively simple improvements can make a noticeable difference. Replacing failing storage, increasing memory, updating outdated systems or improving backup arrangements may resolve problems that employees have been dealing with for months.
Preventive maintenance can also help businesses plan their spending. Instead of unexpectedly replacing several computers after failures occur, a company can gradually identify which equipment is approaching the end of its useful life and budget for replacements accordingly.
Computer Repair Should Be Part of a Wider IT Strategy
For businesses, fixing a damaged computer is only one part of maintaining a dependable technology environment. The more important question is whether the repair fits into the company’s wider IT requirements.
Computer Repair can address issues such as failing hardware, slow performance, damaged components and software-related problems, but businesses may also need support with networks, backups, security and cloud platforms.
For example, repairing a workstation without addressing an unstable network may solve one problem while leaving another source of downtime untouched. Similarly, replacing a failed computer without reviewing the company’s backup process could create unnecessary data risks in the future.
A broader IT strategy helps connect these individual areas. It allows businesses to consider how devices are maintained, how information is protected and how employees access the systems they need to work effectively.
Managed Services Can Change the Way Businesses Handle IT
As businesses grow, managing technology entirely on an ad hoc basis can become increasingly difficult. More employees mean more devices, more accounts, more software and more potential points of failure.
Managed services provide a more structured way to oversee an organisation’s IT environment. Instead of waiting for every issue to become an emergency, businesses can have ongoing support and monitoring designed around their particular requirements.
For a small business without a full-time internal IT department, this can be especially useful. Routine technical responsibilities can be handled alongside troubleshooting and strategic planning, allowing employees to concentrate on their primary work.
Managed services can also provide a clearer understanding of the business’s technology needs over time. A business may initially require basic support, but as it grows it could need improved networking, stronger security, better backups, Microsoft 365 management or additional cloud resources.
Cloud Services Are Now Part of Everyday Business Operations
Cloud technology has changed the way many businesses store information and access applications. Employees can work with documents, email, collaboration platforms and business software without everything being dependent on a single computer or physical office server.
However, moving services into the cloud does not remove the need for proper IT management. Cloud accounts still need to be configured correctly, access permissions need to be controlled and businesses need to understand how their information is protected and backed up.
Well-managed cloud services can provide flexibility for businesses with employees working across different locations. They can also make it easier for authorised users to access information when working remotely or from another office.
At the same time, businesses should avoid assuming that every cloud service automatically solves their backup and security requirements. A reliable IT strategy should consider how important information is stored, who can access it and what happens if an account is compromised or data is accidentally deleted.
A Reliable Network Supports the Entire Workplace
Computers depend on more than their individual hardware. A reliable network is essential when employees need to share files, access cloud platforms, use printers, communicate internally or connect to business applications.
Network problems can be particularly disruptive because a single issue may affect multiple employees at the same time. A poorly configured wireless network, outdated equipment or unstable connection can create slowdowns that are difficult to diagnose from an individual computer.
Businesses should therefore consider networking as part of their wider IT environment rather than treating it as a separate technical concern. Proper configuration, secure wireless access, appropriate network equipment and regular maintenance can help create a more dependable workplace.
For businesses operating across Western Sydney, having access to local technical expertise can also make a difference when onsite assistance is required. Local support can be particularly useful when an issue involves physical equipment, office networking or a workstation that cannot easily be diagnosed remotely.
Security and Backups Should Be Part of the Same Conversation
A computer that works perfectly but has inadequate security or backup arrangements can still present a serious business risk.
Businesses routinely hold customer information, financial records, internal documents and other valuable data. Hardware failure, accidental deletion, malware or other incidents can make that information unavailable at the worst possible time.
Regular backups provide an additional layer of protection, but businesses should also consider whether backups can actually be restored when needed. A backup that has never been tested may not provide the reassurance a business expects.
Security should similarly be approached as an ongoing process. Software updates, account protection, antivirus solutions, secure passwords and appropriate access controls can all contribute to a safer technology environment.
The goal is not to make a business completely immune to every possible problem. Rather, it is to reduce unnecessary exposure and ensure that the organisation has sensible recovery options when something does go wrong.
The Right Repair Decision Is Not Always Replacement
When a computer develops a problem, replacing it immediately may seem like the easiest solution. However, that is not necessarily the most economical choice.
Some issues can be resolved through relatively simple repairs or upgrades. A failing drive, insufficient memory or damaged component may be replaceable without requiring the business to purchase an entirely new system.
On the other hand, an older computer that has become increasingly unreliable may no longer justify continued repair costs. If it is also incompatible with modern software or lacks the performance required for the employee’s role, replacement may be the better long-term decision.
Professional assessment helps businesses make that distinction. Instead of spending money based purely on assumptions, business owners can consider the age, condition, performance and role of each device before deciding what to do.
How Australian Businesses Can Build More Reliable IT
Technology should support business growth rather than become another source of daily frustration. That requires more than responding whenever a computer fails. Businesses can benefit from looking at their technology as a connected environment in which computers, networks, cloud platforms, security systems and data protection all contribute to productivity.
A practical approach also recognises that every business is different. A small office may have completely different requirements from a multi-location company, while a professional services firm may rely on different systems from a retail or manufacturing business.
Businesses should therefore focus on solutions that match their actual operations. Reliable computer maintenance, sensible upgrades, managed services, secure cloud systems and dependable networking can work together to create an IT environment that is easier to manage and less likely to cause avoidable disruption.
For companies in and around Penrith, Richmond, Windsor and wider Western Sydney, this can be especially important as more everyday business functions become dependent on connected technology. Local businesses can benefit from having support available for both immediate technical problems and longer-term technology planning.
Frequently Asked Questions
How often should a business have its computers checked?
There is no single schedule that suits every company. Businesses with older equipment, heavy workloads or critical systems may benefit from more frequent checks. Regular monitoring and maintenance can help identify performance, storage, security and software problems before they result in significant downtime.
Is repairing a business computer better than replacing it?
It depends on the age, condition and performance of the computer. A relatively modern machine with a replaceable faulty component may be worth repairing, while an older device with repeated problems may be more economical to replace. A professional assessment can help determine which option makes more sense.
Can IT support help prevent computer downtime?
Yes. Regular maintenance, monitoring, software updates, hardware assessments, backups and network management can reduce the likelihood of avoidable failures. The objective is to identify potential issues early rather than waiting until they interrupt normal business operations.
Why are managed services useful for small businesses?
Managed services can give small businesses access to ongoing IT support without necessarily requiring a large internal technology team. They can help with routine maintenance, monitoring, security, cloud systems and troubleshooting while allowing employees to focus on their normal responsibilities.
Do cloud services eliminate the need for local IT support?
No. Cloud platforms can reduce dependence on physical infrastructure, but businesses still need to manage accounts, permissions, security, backups, connectivity and integrations. IT support remains useful for ensuring these systems work together effectively.
What should businesses do if a computer keeps experiencing the same problem?
Repeated failures should not simply be treated as separate incidents. The underlying cause should be investigated. It could be ageing hardware, software compatibility, insufficient resources, overheating, network issues or another recurring problem. Identifying the root cause can help prevent the same disruption from happening again.
Final Thoughts
Reliable technology is one of the foundations of modern business productivity. When computers, networks and cloud systems work as expected, employees can focus on customers and completing their responsibilities instead of spending valuable working hours dealing with technical problems.
Professional support can provide more value when it goes beyond emergency troubleshooting. By combining maintenance, business computer work, managed services, cloud services, networking, security and sensible hardware decisions, businesses can create an IT environment that is more dependable and easier to manage.
For Australian businesses, the goal should not simply be to keep computers running. It should be to build technology systems that support the way the business operates today while remaining flexible enough to accommodate future growth. A practical approach to IT can reduce unnecessary downtime, protect productivity and give business owners greater confidence in the systems they rely on every day.

articles.title: Airtel bats for sovereign stack to process data from India
articles.text:
Airtel bats for sovereign stack to process data from India
According to Airtel it would be incorrect to equate local data residency with data sovereignty as it is about controlling the data with a sovereign technology stack.
Bharti Airtel has questioned the fragmented approach in current rules to allow data processing of Indians overseas and has pushed for control on local data using sovereign cloud, a senior company official has said.
Speaking at Global Fintech Fest 2026, Bharti Airtel, Group CRO and Director of Corporate Affairs, Rahul Vatts said it is not correct to equate local data residency with data sovereignty but it is about controlling the data with a sovereign technology stack.
He said the government came up with the first circular on this, which is actually quite pathbreaking "and the government has had very detailed discussions over the last 30-45 days as to what we should be really looking at".
He said while the government remains proactive, two areas that should always be important for us to keep, one is to have a clear discussion on where the control plane is and the manner in which it will be managed.
"The second part is that we need to get away from this fragmented policy approach. For example, the government today says that critical government data sets should be under sovereign ground. But why not for the energy data, health record, the identities of people? I think this policy approach has to be consistent so that we cover the entire universe of what is critical to us," he said.
Vatts said as sectoral regulators begin issuing their own enabling guidelines, the question for critical workloads is no longer just about the selection of any cloud, but a careful evaluation of which cloud architecture guarantees end-to-end control under Indian law.
Airtel is in the process of building a couple of 100-megawatt data centres over the next couple of years and is betting big on demand for sovereign cloud infrastructure required for strategic reasons in the country.
Vatts said India is already generating the largest data per consumer.
"We are already hitting around 38-40 GB per month per customer. And a lot of predictions now take us towards 7075 GB per customer in the next 3-4 years. So you are already generating a humongous amount of data," he said.

articles.title: Nepal tiene una nueva atracción en Google Maps. La casa verde que sobrevivió a la riada cuyo secreto está enterrado bajo tierra
articles.text:
En medio de un paisaje arrasado por la riada en Nepal, una imagen terminó haciéndose viral: una casa verde permanecía en pie mientras buena parte de lo que había a su alrededor había desaparecido. La vivienda de la familia Pyakurel se convirtió en la “Miracle House”, atrajo visitantes y terminó incluso señalada en Google Maps como una atracción “resistente a inundaciones”.
Pero la explicación más interesante podría no estar a la vista.
Una casa en pie. Contaba el New York Times que la familia Pyakurel estaba en su vivienda de Dhunge Bazaar cuando una enorme corriente de agua, barro y escombros alcanzó la zona después del colapso del glaciar en la región del Himalaya entre Nepal y el Tíbet.
Durante más de una hora contemplaron desde el tercer piso y posteriormente desde el tejado cómo el agua golpeaba el edificio y destruía lo que encontraba a su alrededor. Cuando el nivel comenzó a descender, unos vecinos utilizaron tuberías metálicas para improvisar una escalera y sacar a la familia. La casa, contra todo pronóstico, seguía en pie.
Desaparecieron casas, carreteras y hasta un bazar. La excepcionalidad de la vivienda se entiende mejor observando lo que quedó a su alrededor: barro, escombros y enormes extensiones donde antes había edificios e infraestructuras. En el distrito de Nuwakot, más de 1.200 viviendas quedaron completamente destruidas y otras mil sufrieron daños parciales, mientras puentes y tramos enteros de carreteras desaparecieron.
Cerca de la casa, las turbinas eléctricas situadas al otro lado del río fueron arrastradas, un bazar entero dejó de existir y cuatro viviendas pertenecientes a una misma familia desaparecieron, incluida una tan nueva que sus propietarios todavía no se habían mudado.
Una atracción en Maps. Las fotografías de aquella construcción verde prácticamente aislada entre la destrucción comenzaron a circular por las redes sociales hasta el punto que la vivienda recibió rápidamente dos apodos: la “Miracle House” y la “Viral House”.
Cuando la carretera volvió a abrir parcialmente, comenzaron a llegar curiosos hasta Dhunge Bazaar para observarla desde una elevación y hacerse fotografías con ella. La fama digital llegó aún más lejos: el lugar consiguió su propio marcador en Google Maps como una atracción “flood-proof”, convirtiendo una vivienda familiar en uno de los símbolos más insólitos de la catástrofe.
El (posible) secreto. Es la gran pregunta, y Chhatra Bahadur Pyakurel, patriarca de la familia, cree que existe una explicación estructural para que su casa resistiera donde otras desaparecieron: sus pilares fueron anclados perforando profundamente hasta alcanzar la roca. La planta baja había sido construida en 1995 para albergar su tienda de alimentación y, a medida que prosperó el negocio familiar, fueron añadiendo nuevas plantas sobre aquella estructura.
También se ha planteado otra posible explicación: una cresta situada frente a la trayectoria de la corriente pudo actuar parcialmente como escudo, por lo que no existe todavía una demostración técnica de que los cimientos fueran por sí solos responsables de la supervivencia.
Lo que no sobrevivió. La imagen de la casa intacta es engañosa porque las dos primeras plantas sufrieron daños: apenas permanecieron elementos estructurales, mientras el agua destruyó posesiones y documentos familiares tan importantes como pasaportes, certificados de ciudadanía y títulos de propiedad.
En cambio, en el tercer piso seguían visibles una lavadora y ropa, y en el tejado permanecían depósitos de agua, un calentador solar, plantas e incluso un pequeño templo familiar. Para Pyakurel, sin embargo, la verdadera suerte no fue que sobreviviera el edificio: su nieto había salido poco antes hacia el colegio, situado en una zona elevada, y toda la familia consiguió reunirse sana y salva al día siguiente.

articles.title: Bajar la tapa al tirar de la cadena no es la solución definitiva: esto es lo que dice la ciencia sobre los aerosoles del inodoro
articles.text:
Uno de los consejos más importantes que escuchamos con respecto a la higiene de nuestro hogar es lo importante que es bajar la tapa del inodoro antes de tirar de la cadena. Y la idea es bastante sencilla, porque se busca evitar que una nube invisible de bacterias y partículas, conocida como "pluma del inodoro" inunde nuestro baño y, por ende, todo lo que hay a su alrededor.
El viaje invisible. Dentro de los diferentes científicos que se han hecho, no hay debate en torno a que la descarga genera gotas y partículas suspendidas en el aire. Y si el agua que hay en el inodoro tiene microorganismos, se pueden generar bioaerosoles.
Lo que ha llamado la atención de los investigadores es el alcance de estas partículas, puesto que algunos estudios detectaron que estos aerosoles alcanzan alturas compatibles con la zona de respiración de un adulto. Además, se ha comprobado que ciertas partículas pueden permanecer suspendidas en el aire durante al menos 20 segundos tras la descarga.
Depende del inodoro. La cantidad de aerosoles que se disparan por el baño no es siempre la misma, puesto que los principales factores de riesgo demostrados son una mayor carga microbiana en el agua y el uso de inodoros con grandes volúmenes de descarga. De hecho, los modelos de inodoros de alta energía generan una mayor cantidad de aerosoles que los modelos más eficientes.
El mito de la tapa. Con lo último que conocemos, no tenemos las pruebas necesarias para afirmar de manera categórica que bajar la tapa, la ventilación del baño y la presión de descarga sean factores fundamentales para poder reducir nuestra exposición. Es cierto que estudios clásicos, como uno de 2012 con la bacteria Clostridioides difficile, demostraron que bajar la tapa reducía la dispersión de las gotas más grandes y disminuía la contaminación de las superficies.
Sin embargo, simulaciones recientes de dinámica de fluidos sugieren que la tapa actúa como un arma de doble filo. Si bien cerrar la tapa puede reducir la exposición de personas que se encuentren alejadas, también puede modificar la trayectoria de las partículas, aumentando la exposición de quien esté situado muy cerca del inodoro en ese momento.
Una idea. Con todo esto, la idea de que cerrar la tapa elimina por completo los aerosoles es excesiva, puesto que simplemente los reduce o los redirige. Y con la ventilación ocurre algo parecido, puesto que un estudio en baños públicos señaló que la falta de ventilación y la alta ocupación favorecen la acumulación de partículas. Asimismo, la persistencia de bioaerosoles depende del tiempo transcurrido, la distancia y la ventilación mecánica. Pero la ventilación por sí sola no elimina mágicamente el riesgo, sino que reduce la concentración o altera la dispersión dependiendo del diseño del espacio.
Las enfermedades. Si las partículas pueden llegar a nuestro aparato respiratorio, lo lógico es pensar que los inodoros son un foco constante de contagio. Pero la realidad es bastante diferente, puesto que, aunque las pruebas apuntan a que la descarga genera aerosoles, no demuestra que esto cause habitualmente infecciones en las personas.
De hecho, una revisión ya señaló años atrás que no se había demostrado (ni descartado por completo) la transmisión de enfermedades por estos aerosoles en condiciones reales de la vida cotidiana. Pero aquí hay que recordar que no es lo mismo detectar contaminación en un entorno experimental cerrado que probar que eso se traduce en infecciones reales para los usuarios.

articles.title: Pendant les French Days, il y a des réductions sur les offres Nord VPN et 4 mois offerts
articles.text:
Un VPN permet de naviguer en toute confidentialité sur vos appareils connectés, et parmi les fournisseurs, NordVPN est sans doute le plus connu d’entre eux. Il propose de temps à autre des promotions sur l’ensemble de ses abonnements, avec un ou plusieurs mois offerts. Les French Days sont encore une occasion de proposer ses formules à moindre coût.
- L’abonnement Basique de deux ans est proposé au prix de 3,37 € par mois, ou 94,23 € pour les 28 premiers mois, au lieu de 324,52 €.
- L’abonnement Premium, le plus populaire chez le fournisseur, est au prix de 4,33 € par mois, ou 121,23 € pour 28 mois, au lieu de 512,12 €.
- Enfin, l’abonnement Ultime Max, qui est le plus complet, comprend les utilitaires NordPass et NordLocker au prix de 8,19 € par mois, ou 229,23 € pour 28 mois, au lieu de 789,32 € habituellement.
C’est quoi, NordVPN ?
NordVPN
Le VPN que tout le monde connaît
- Interface simple et lisible
- Serveurs rapides
- Bonnes performances
- Fonctionnalités variées
- Application facile à utiliser
Un VPN permet de masquer son adresse IP et de protéger les données échangées lors de sa navigation sur Internet. NordVPN ne se cantonne pas aux ordinateurs : le service fonctionne aussi sur Android, macOS et iOS, ainsi que sur certains téléviseurs connectés. Pour assurer la connexion, le fournisseur utilise notamment le protocole NordLynx, qui mise sur la rapidité sans faire l’impasse sur la sécurité. Son réseau de serveurs permet également de profiter de débits élevés et d’un ping stable, un point important pour le streaming, les téléchargements ou encore les jeux en ligne.
NordVPN dispose de plusieurs milliers de serveurs répartis à travers le monde, avec plus de 8 400 serveurs dans plus de 167 pays selon le fournisseur. L’application permet de sélectionner facilement le pays ou le serveur auquel se connecter, mais il est aussi possible de laisser NordVPN choisir automatiquement le serveur le plus adapté. L’interface reste plutôt sobre, mais suffisamment claire pour s’y retrouver rapidement : quelques clics suffisent pour établir la connexion et naviguer avec une adresse IP différente.
À ce prix, les abonnements NordVPN sont-ils une bonne affaire ?
NordVPN fait partie des références du marché des VPN. L’offre est d’autant plus intéressante qu’elle inclut actuellement quatre mois supplémentaires. En plus de sécuriser la connexion, le service propose plusieurs fonctionnalités pratiques, comme Meshnet et le split tunneling, qui permet de choisir les applications qui utilisent ou non le VPN. On retrouve également un kill switch : en cas de coupure de la connexion au serveur VPN, celui-ci bloque automatiquement l’accès à Internet afin d’éviter que l’adresse IP réelle ne soit exposée.
Les différentes formules ne donnent toutefois pas toutes accès aux mêmes services. NordPass, le gestionnaire de mots de passe de NordVPN, est réservé aux abonnements Premium et Ultime Max. L’offre Ultime Max ajoute également NordLocker, un espace de stockage cloud conçu pour conserver ses fichiers dans un coffre-fort numérique sécurisé.
Quelles sont les dates des French Days ?
En 2026, les French Days de la rentrée se déroulent du 7 septembre au 14 septembre inclus. Comme pour le Black Friday, de nouvelles promotions peuvent tomber chaque jour même si la plupart des commerçants proposent d’entrée de jeu leurs meilleures promotions.
