articles.title: Why MCP security is about permissions overhaul
articles.text:
Why MCP security is about permissions overhaul
Anthropic’s Model Context Protocol (MCP) went into production in late 2024. It spread rapidly after that.
Since then, thousands of MCP servers have been created. Microsoft, Google, and OpenAI embraced it. The Linux Foundation took over protocol maintenance. Today, MCP is considered critical infrastructure. It sits between an AI agent and the tools and data it interacts with. Most teams implemented it the same way they implement any other integration standard. People installed it and trusted the defaults.
The understanding that emerged in 2026 is that the problem wasn’t in the infrastructure. The problem is in the permissions below this infrastructure.
This matters because it changes how people approach MCP security problems. A patch solves a specific problem on a particular server. The permission change requires asking a complicated question.
“The understanding that emerged in 2026 is that the problem wasn’t in the infrastructure. The problem is in the permissions below this infrastructure.”
Why did that particular server require access to something it never needed to be there? According to the SANS 2026 Identity Threats Survey, which surveyed more than 500 security experts, 76 percent of businesses noted an increase in non-human identities. 74 percent of businesses use AI systems that rely on standing credentials to work independently. This same survey revealed that none of the protection measures, such as approval processes, sandboxing, or logging, is used by more than 40 percent of businesses.
Look past the individual disclosures, and the same root cause keeps showing up. In May 2025, an attacker used prompt injection against the GitHub MCP server to pull private repository data, not because the server had a bug in the traditional sense, but because the personal access token behind it was scoped far wider than the task required. Days later, a logic flaw in an Asana MCP integration allowed cross-tenant access because the permission layer never enforced the isolation boundary between customers.
Security researchers now group it under a couple of recognizable patterns: tool poisoning, where a server’s own tool description carries hidden instructions, and the confused deputy problem, where an agent inherits more trust than the task in front of it requires.
What a permissions redesign actually asks you to check
The solution that keeps coming up isn’t a better scanner, but compartmentalizing access. GitHub’s Engineering Blog, which discusses developing secure remote MCP servers, suggests the following: every instance must have its own secrets for the specific task, all requests must be limited to the acting user, and authorization must be based on action rather than assumed after user authentication. Replace fixed, permanent tokens with dynamic, temporary credentials generated on the fly.
“Replace fixed, permanent tokens with dynamic, temporary credentials generated on the fly.”
This solution is tiered and has been working until now. In Webflow, we treat MCP integrations in the same way as we treat other third-party components with access to customer data.
Each credential the team gives to an AI agent was probably a good idea when it was provisioned. The tough call isn’t whether that access was a good idea at the time. It’s whether it is anymore, and most teams aren’t in the habit of making it.
Some things to consider while integrating any MCP:
What can this credential reach now, rather than the scope for which it was intended? The scope of access is likely to creep. No review will be scheduled until something breaks.
Is authorization granted on a per-site, per-repository, or per-Workspace basis, or all or nothing? Be leery of any integration that only provides organizational access. If an integration doesn’t give you control over scope at connection time, that’s the finding, not a footnote.
Does the AI agent inherit the person’s existing credentials, or create entirely new credentials that bypass those permissions? The latter is how a GitHub personal access token can have more access to repos than the user who authorized it.
Does logging assign accountability for what the agent does in the same way it does for a human? If the agent’s activities are invisible or unattributable, incident response starts at ground zero.
Do changes from the agent go straight into production, or do they pass through a reviewable process like draft, branch, and approval queue first? This is just applying the security discipline the team already has around human access controls to a newer class of entity.
Identity comes before access
Before you can talk about what an agent is allowed to do, you have to answer a harder question: what is an agent, identity-wise? Right now the honest answer for most of the industry is “a human’s OAuth token wearing a trenchcoat.” The agent doesn’t have its own identity. It inherits the scope, the blast radius, and often the literal credential of whoever spun it up.
That’s a problem the moment agents stop being ephemeral. Most agents today live for minutes to hours: a task starts, the agent runs, it dies. But that’s changing. We’re heading toward agents that run for weeks or months, and a thing that lives that long needs its own identity, not a borrowed one, with permissions that get stricter, not looser, as the lifespan grows.
“Right now the honest answer for most of the industry is ‘a human’s OAuth token wearing a trenchcoat.'”
Think of it like the difference between a contractor you bring in for an afternoon and a contingent worker embedded in your systems for a quarter. You wouldn’t give the afternoon contractor a permanent badge, and you shouldn’t give the quarter-long agent the same access as a five-minute script.
OAuth wasn’t built for this, and it’s not just a missing feature; it’s a structural mismatch, and at root a UX failure: a consent model built for a human in the loop, applied to a process that has none.
Its whole model assumes a human sits in front of a scope dialog and makes an informed choice, and we all know how that goes: nobody reads the scope list; they click allow. That already-shaky assumption collapses completely when there’s no human reading anything.
The base spec has no concept of “this client is an agent” or “this grant is expected to run for six months,” just a server-set expiry after the fact. A few IETF drafts are starting to sketch a fix: binding token lifetime to a task’s actual lifecycle and tagging agents with stable identities distinct from the human who invoked them. Still, those are early-stage proposals, not deployed standard(s).
We don’t have a clean answer for where the line sits between “short-lived task, broad-ish access” and “long-lived agent, locked down tight.” Webflow’s security team is actively working through this, and we’re comparing notes with peers across the industry rather than pretending we’ve solved it. But the framing itself matters: treat agent lifespan as a first-class input to your permission model, not an afterthought.
Permissions aren’t a checkbox at provisioning
A permissions redesign, a protocol update, and an identity model represent three distinct levels of the same problem. For each level to remain effective, the other two must be effective too.
If you create a credential with the correct scope on Day One, but then no one ever verifies that the credential remains valid, your efforts were wasted. Similarly, if you develop a new protocol that finally distinguishes an agent from the human behind it, but all integrations continue to provide standing, all-or-nothing access by default, you have done little good. Neither approach addresses the deeper question at the root of both: what an agent is permitted to do should depend on how long it will exist.
“The teams who get this right will be the teams who stopped viewing scope, identity, and lifetime as three separate evaluations, and began treating them as a single setting.”
Right now, nearly all components of the technology stack don’t know how to ask that question, much less answer it. The teams who get this right will not be the ones who developed a more efficient scanning tool. Rather, they will be the teams who stopped viewing scope, identity, and lifetime as three separate evaluations that occur once per agent instance, and began treating them as a single setting that must be evaluated each time the agent’s function or existence changes.
This article was originally published on September 9, 2026, on webflow.com.

articles.title: Un error de Meta revela sus próximas gafas de realidad mixta para sustituir a las Quest Pro
articles.text:
Meta ha dejado al descubierto por error el diseño de sus próximas gafas de realidad mixta, conocidas internamente como Project Phoenix. Una actualización del firmware de Horizon OS incorporó imágenes del dispositivo, revelando por primera vez su aspecto final antes de que la compañía lo presente oficialmente.
Las imágenes aparecieron después de que Meta actualizara una aplicación llamada HorizonOS Prescription Lens, disponible en la Horizon Store. El programa fue creado para facilitar la configuración de lentes graduadas compatibles con las nuevas gafas, pero su distribución permitió acceder a archivos internos que contenían imágenes del dispositivo.
PUBLICIDAD
La filtración confirma además algunos detalles que ya habían circulado sobre Phoenix y muestra que Meta está preparando un producto de gama alta con un diseño muy diferente al de sus actuales visores Quest.
Una aplicación de Meta dejó al descubierto las gafas
El origen de la filtración se remonta a semanas atrás, cuando Meta publicó la aplicación HorizonOS Prescription Lens. A diferencia de una aplicación convencional, su contenido podía revisarse mediante un archivo ZIP distribuido durante la instalación.
PUBLICIDAD
La primera versión apenas contenía elementos relevantes. Sin embargo, una actualización publicada en septiembre incorporó imágenes que muestran cómo se colocan y retiran las lentes graduadas del dispositivo.
Las capturas también enseñan el procedimiento para configurar las gafas mediante un código QR. En una de ellas aparece un usuario acercando el código a los sensores del dispositivo para completar la configuración.
PUBLICIDAD
Phoenix tendrá un diseño más parecido al de unas gafas
Uno de los detalles más llamativos de las imágenes es el diseño. Project Phoenix no adopta el aspecto voluminoso de los visores Quest y tampoco es una versión de las Meta Ray-Ban.
Meta apuesta en este caso por un dispositivo más delgado y abierto, con almohadillas nasales similares a las de unas gafas convencionales. El puente de la nariz podrá ajustarse tanto en altura como en separación, además de incorporar piezas de diferentes tamaños para adaptarse al rostro.
PUBLICIDAD
Las imágenes también muestran sensores situados en los laterales y en la zona inferior de las patillas. En la parte posterior se aprecia el cable que conecta el dispositivo con un puck de cómputo externo, situado en el extremo de la patilla izquierda.
Un visor pensado para competir en la gama alta
De acuerdo con la información publicada por UploadVR, Phoenix ocuparía el espacio de gama alta que Meta dejó vacante tras la discontinuación de Quest Pro.
PUBLICIDAD
Aunque su diseño será diferente, el funcionamiento seguirá basándose en el concepto de realidad mixta utilizado por dispositivos como Quest 3 y Quest 3S. El visor combinará elementos digitales con una representación del entorno real mediante cámaras, una tecnología conocida como passthrough.
En cuanto a las pantallas, Project Phoenix utilizaría paneles micro-OLED con una resolución de 2560 × 2560 píxeles por ojo. Esta configuración ofrecería una mayor densidad de píxeles que Quest 3, aunque seguiría por debajo de las Apple Vision Pro. A cambio, el campo de visión sería más reducido, pero con una imagen potencialmente más nítida.
PUBLICIDAD
El proyecto nació tras la cancelación de Quest Pro 2
El desarrollo de Phoenix estaría relacionado con la decisión de Meta de cancelar el sucesor directo de Quest Pro. Andrew Bosworth, director de tecnología de Meta, explicó anteriormente que el elevado coste de las pantallas utilizadas en aquel proyecto fue uno de los factores que llevaron a cancelar su desarrollo.
El nuevo dispositivo buscaría ofrecer una alternativa de gama alta mediante otro planteamiento de diseño y hardware.
Entre sus componentes también se menciona un chip Snapdragon Reality Elite de Qualcomm, que podría estar integrado directamente en las gafas o alojado en el dispositivo externo encargado del procesamiento.
PUBLICIDAD
Meta podría presentar Phoenix este mes
Por ahora, Meta no ha confirmado oficialmente el precio ni la fecha de lanzamiento de Project Phoenix. Sin embargo, todo apunta a que podría convertirse en uno de los anuncios importantes de Meta Connect 2026, cuya celebración está prevista para comenzar el 23 de septiembre.
El precio será uno de los principales interrogantes. Las Quest Pro llegaron al mercado con un precio de 1.500 dólares, aunque Meta posteriormente redujo su costo en 500 dólares antes de discontinuarlas.
PUBLICIDAD
Si Phoenix ocupa realmente el espacio de gama alta de la compañía, es probable que su precio se sitúe muy por encima de las Quest convencionales. Por ahora, la filtración permite conocer su diseño antes de que Meta revele oficialmente todos sus detalles.
PUBLICIDAD
PUBLICIDAD

articles.title: IKEA releases new Skyrim mod that adds gloriously mundane Kallax shelving unit as your newest companion — free collab provides a drab flatpack answer to your loot woes
articles.text:
IKEA releases new Skyrim mod that adds gloriously mundane Kallax shelving unit as your newest companion — free collab provides a drab flatpack answer to your loot woes
But in the long history of bizarre and meme Skyrim mods, this IKEA effort isn’t that strange.
IKEA has announced the Kallax Storageborn companion creation for players of The Elder Scrolls V: Skyrim Special Edition on PC or Xbox. But who’d want a set of drab utilitarian Swedish shelves following them around during their adventures in this fantastical role-playing game? The answer is quite a lot of people, it would seem, from the social media feedback we’ve seen. IKEA’s free mod for this iconic RPG also appeals to gamers’ pragmatic instincts with its claims that “your inventory woes end here.”
The household furniture giant says it designed this Skyrim mod as it wanted to bring its real world smart storage solutions to the digital domain. Skyrim was chosen, in particular, because gamers in this classic title are “plagued by the evils of encumbrance and disorganization,” asserts IKEA.
Of course, the furniture maker will have invested time and money into the development of this fully voiced companion mod (voiced by comic actor Matt Berry) for the publicity, too. But there's little to complain about as it's free and entirely optional to your Skyrim experience.
If you are interested in adding the Kallax Storageborn companion creation to your Skyrim experience, you can get it directly from Bethesda here, for free. But before using these eminently practical flatpack DIY shelves in your game and “sending clutter back to the fires of oblivion,” you have to discover and assemble your Kallax through a questline. You’ll find it at the Dwemer furniture store, where you’ll also discover the secrets of Kallax’s origin and have to defeat the Clutter Golem.
Naturally, you summon this shelving unit in the game with a call of ‘Aya Key Yah.”
The mod doesn’t just introduce your trusty new Kallax Storageborn companion; you’ll also get access to the Allenblade weapon, some blue and yellow-themed armor, and a Meatball helmet.
It is always interesting to see non-tech brands cross over into our reporting realm. The first example that springs to mind is the KFC console, but IKEA has dipped its toe into tech more recently by expanding its computer furniture ranges to include products such as the Xbox Gaming Den furniture series showcased at Gamescom 2026, plus various smart home accessories.

Mark Tyson is a news editor at Tom's Hardware. He enjoys covering the full breadth of PC tech; from business and semiconductor design to products approaching the edge of reason.

articles.title: Melhor fone de ouvido Philips: 10 modelos que valem a pena em 2026 • Tecnoblog
articles.text:
Melhor fone de ouvido Philips: 10 modelos que valem a pena em 2026
Encontre fones de ouvido Philips para o seu dia a dia; lista inclui modelos Bluetooth e com fio, com ANC, bateria duradoura e preço acessível
Os fones de ouvido da Philips são conhecidos pelo preço acessível, e atendem a propostas diferentes. A marca vende desde headphones com cancelamento ativo de ruído (ANC) até opções TWS compactas e dispositivos de construção aberta.
Neste guia, o Tecnoblog reuniu 10 fones Philips que valem a pena em 2026. Conheça as principais características de cada produto, além de prós e contras, antes de escolher o melhor para o seu dia a dia.
O TAH6509BK/00 é um fone over-ear que utiliza cancelamento ativo de ruído adaptativo com microfones internos e externos para identificar o ruído e ajustar o cancelamento em tempo real. Há ainda o modo ambiente que permite ouvir os sons externos, e o Quick Awareness, para facilitar conversas sem precisar retirar o fone.
Na reprodução, o headphone traz drivers dinâmicos de 40 mm, sistema acústico fechado e o recurso “Dynamic Bass”, que reforça as baixas frequências sem depender do aumento do volume. Sua autonomia chega a 70h com o cancelamento desligado e 45 horas com o ANC ativado, segundo a marca.
No geral, a conexão sem fio é feita por Bluetooth 5.3, com suporte ao codec SBC e multiponto para manter dois dispositivos conectados simultaneamente. O modelo também pode ser utilizado por cabo USB-C e possui entrada de áudio de 2,5 mm.
Codecs suportados: SBC
O SHP9500 é um headphone analógico com fio (drivers de 50 mm de neodímio e resposta de 12 Hz a 35 kHz) que promete som natural, grave encorpado e sem distorções. Ele conta com cabo destacável de três metros e adaptador P2/P6,3, facilitando a conexão com equipamentos de áudio profissionais.
Com cerca de 320 g, o SHP9500 é mais direcionado a quem pretende ouvir música em casa, trabalhar com áudio ou utilizar um headphone aberto em sessões mais longas. Ele não possui Bluetooth, bateria, ANC ou microfone integrado.
A ausência desses recursos não é acidental, pois a Philips prioriza uma conexão cabeada e uma arquitetura aberta sem isolamento acústico nesse modelo. Em vez de tentar bloquear o ambiente, as conchas permitem maior interação entre o som reproduzido e o espaço ao redor.
Codecs compatíveis: não se aplica ao modelo.
Para quem procura um TWS com cancelamento de ruído, o TAT3509GY/00 combina ANC adaptativo com um formato intra-auricular. O sistema utiliza cancelamento híbrido e o ajusta de acordo com o ambiente, relevante em locais com barulho constante, como transporte público, escritórios ou ambientes movimentados.
Os dois fones utilizam drivers dinâmicos de 10 mm e conexão Bluetooth 5.3 com suporte a multiponto e sensor infravermelho para pausa automática ao retirar um dos fones.
A autonomia varia de acordo com o uso do ANC: são até oito horas nos fones e 16 horas adicionais pelo estojo com o cancelamento desligado. Com ANC ativado, a estimativa cai para seis horas nos fones e mais 12 horas no estojo. Sua certificação IPX4 é limitada contra respingos e suor, e não protege contra poeira.
O TAT2500BK/00 é um fone intra-auricular que oferece ANC, multiponto e modo de transparência para ouvir o som ambiente. Os drivers dinâmicos têm 8 mm e a marca oferece o recurso Dynamic Bass, que pode ser ativado para reforçar as baixas frequências mesmo em volumes menores.
A conexão utiliza Bluetooth 5.4, com suporte ao aplicativo Philips Headphones para ajustar a equalização e outras configurações. Há também um microfone destinado às chamadas e dois microfones utilizados pelo sistema de ANC.
A bateria chega a seis horas de reprodução nos próprios fones com o ANC desligado, enquanto o estojo acrescenta outras 18 horas. No entanto, a marca não informa a autonomia com o ANC ativado. A certificação IPX4 protege contra respingos de água e suor, assim como no TAT3509GY/00.
Com construção over-ear, o TAH2300BK é voltado a quem prefere um headphone tradicional e não quer depender de recargas. As conchas fechadas ajudam no isolamento passivo, trazendo drivers dinâmicos de 40 mm e um modo Extra Bass, que altera a reprodução para reforçar as frequências graves.
A conectividade sem fio fica por conta do Bluetooth 5.4 e conexão multiponto para manter dois dispositivos conectados simultaneamente, o que pode ser útil para alternar entre computador e celular.
O headphone conta com microfone para chamadas e controles físicos, além de compatibilidade com assistentes de voz. Não há ANC ativo e a bateria integrada de 500 mAh oferece até 55 horas de reprodução, segundo a Philips. Ele não tem certificação IP contra água e poeira.
O TAQ2000BK/00 se diferencia pelo formato aberto com presilha que fica na parte externa da orelha. Em vez de vedar o canal auditivo como um fone intra-auricular, os drivers utilizam condução aérea para direcionar o som — característica que permite perceber o ambiente enquanto se ouve música, o que pode ser útil em caminhadas ou corridas.
A autonomia chega a sete horas por carga, com mais 21 horas fornecidas pelo estojo, segundo a marca. A classificação IPX4 indica proteção contra respingos e suor, mas não contra submersão.
O modelo traz drivers dinâmicos têm 12 mm e Bluetooth 5.4 com conexão multiponto para dois aparelhos simultaneamente, além de recursos como Dynamic Bass que reforça e amplifica os sons graves de músicas.
O TAT1139BK/00 adota um formato open-fit, sem a vedação típica das ponteiras de silicone que entram no canal auditivo. Isso oferece uma sensação mais aberta durante o uso, mas significa que a capacidade de isolamento passivo é menor do que a de modelos intra-auriculares.
O fone traz drivers dinâmicos de 13 mm para reprodução de áudio, Bluetooth 5.4 e microfone com processamento de IA para ligações.
Não há cancelamento ativo de ruído e o modelo tem autonomia para até seis horas de uso dos fones, enquanto o estojo acrescenta outras 20 horas. Ele conta com certificação IPX4, assim como outros modelos deste guia.
O TAH2209BK/00 é um fone com formato on-ear, dobrável e que pesa 141 gramas, ideal para mobilidade e uso prolongado. O áudio é reproduzido por drivers dinâmicos de 32 mm e pode receber reforço de graves por meio do recurso Dynamic Bass.
A transmissão sem fio utiliza Bluetooth 5.4, com codec SBC e multiponto para dois dispositivos. Um microfone integrado ao modelo também permite realizar chamadas sem precisar retirar o headphone.
A bateria proporciona até 25 horas de reprodução e leva aproximadamente duas horas para completar a carga por USB-C. Uma recarga rápida de 15 minutos adiciona cerca de uma hora de uso, de acordo com a Philips.
O TAT1209BK/00 é um fone intra-auricular simples, com drivers dinâmicos de 10 mm e também com recurso de reforço dinâmico de graves. Os fones utilizam ponteiras de silicone, que criam uma vedação física no canal auditivo e ajudam no isolamento passivo, mas não há ANC.
O modelo permite usar somente um dos lados enquanto o outro permanece no estojo, e os controles sensíveis ao toque podem comandar reprodução e chamadas. Há ainda um microfone para chamadas e compatibilidade com assistentes de voz via Bluetooth 5.3.
Cada carga fornece até seis horas de reprodução, enquanto o estojo acrescenta mais 12 horas. O carregamento completo leva cerca de duas horas, e 15 minutos de carga oferecem aproximadamente uma hora adicional. Ele também tem certificação IPX4 contra respingos e suor.
O TAH1108BK é um headphone on-ear compacto, com Bluetooth 5.2 e drivers dinâmicos de neodímio de 30 mm. Por não envolver completamente as orelhas, o isolamento é diferente daquele encontrado em headphones over-ear, e a percepção de sons externos tende a ser maior.
A proposta do modelo é oferecer praticidade: as conchas podem ser dobradas para dentro, reduzindo o espaço ocupado durante o transporte, e os comandos ficam diretamente no fone para controlar volume, reprodução e chamadas.
Ele pesa cerca de 180 gramas e sua bateria chega a 15 horas de reprodução com aproximadamente duas horas de carregamento.
A Philips possui modelos com propostas bastante diferentes, desde TWS compactos até headphones over-ear e opções de construção aberta. Considere o seguinte na hora da compra:
Os fones da Philips atendem a diferentes propostas, desde modelos básicos até headphones com ANC, multiponto e recursos de controle de ruído. A qualidade do fone e os recursos variam bastante entre as linhas, por isso a escolha deve considerar o modelo específico e suas tecnologias, e não apenas a marca.
O TAH6509BK/00 é o melhor fone de ouvido Bluetooth da Philips para quem procura um headphone sem fio com cancelamento ativo de ruído. Ele combina ANC híbrido adaptativo, conexão multiponto e até 45 horas de autonomia com o ANC ligado.
Se você prefere um fone intra-auricular, o Philips TAT3509GY/00 tem recursos semelhantes em um formato menor.
Alguns modelos possuem certificação IP, mas isso não é uma característica presente em toda a linha. Entre os modelos deste guia, os com classificação IPX4 tem limitações contra água e suor, sendo inferiores a fones com certificação IP54, IP55 ou IP68 de marcas como Apple e Samsung.
Para saber se um fone é original você deve combinar informações do próprio produto com a procedência da compra. Observe o seguinte:
Não é possível definir qual fone é melhor pois as duas marcas têm modelos de diferentes categorias e faixas de preço. A escolha deve considerar recursos específicos, como ANC, autonomia de bateria, resistência à água, formato e conectividade, já que os melhores fones da Philco também têm especificações avançadas e limitações técnicas.

articles.title: Ig Nobelpreis: Vergrabene Unterhosen enthüllen, wie es dem Boden geht - auch in deinem Garten
articles.text:
Projekt der Uni Zürich: Warum diese Unterhosen etwas über deinen Garten verraten können
Ein Postpaket mit Unterhosen und Teebeuteln zu befüllen, gehört sicherlich nicht zu den typischen Aufgaben in einem Forscher:innenleben. Doch für ein Team der Universität Zürich und Agroscope, das Kompetenzzentrum des Schweizer Bundesamtes für Landwirtschaft, sollte genau dieser Prozess schließlich zu einer der wohl skurrilsten Auszeichnungen in der Wissenschaftscommunity verhelfen. Für ihre Studie „Die Bewertung der Bodengesundheit durch die Verwendung von Baumwollunterhosen mit der Hilfe von 1000 Citizen Scientists“ erhielten Marcel van der Heijden vom Institut für Evolutionsbiologie und Umweltwissenschaften der Uni Zürich, Franz Bender von Agroscope und das Team aus Forschenden und Freiwilligen am 3. September 2026 einen der „Ig Nobelpreise“. Der Award ehrt jährlich Forschung, die „erst zum Lachen und dann zu Nachdenken“ anregen soll, wie es in der Selbstbeschreibung des Preises heißt. Im vergangenen Jahr sorgten italienische Physiker für Aufsehen, da sie die perfekte Formel für ein römisches Pastagericht herausfanden.
Gerade wegen des Einbezugs von Interessierten – auch ohne wissenschaftlichen Background – lohnt es, sich die diesjährig ausgezeichnete Untersuchung der Schweizer:innen näher anzuschauen. Franz Bender von Agroscope erklärt, was man über die vergrabenen und wieder ausgebuddelten Unterhosen lernen kann. Hinter dem ungewöhnlichen Ansatz steckt nämlich eine pfiffige Idee, an der weiterhin Freiwillige teilnehmen und etwas über ihren heimischen Garten erfahren können.
MIT Technology Review: Wie reagierten Unbeteiligten, wenn Sie erzählten, dass Sie für Ihr Forschungsprojekt Unterhosen vergraben (lassen)?
Franz Bender: Die meisten schauen zunächst ungläubig. Danach lächeln sie und dann fragen sie in der Regel „Warum?“. Dann haben wir das Interesse geweckt und können ihnen erzählen, wie wichtig der Boden für uns und unseren Planeten ist und sie zum Mitmachen bewegen.
Wie sind Sie auf die Idee gekommen, Baumwollunterhosen als Gradmesser für die Bodenqualität und den Nährstoffgehalt zu nutzen? Reichen Bodenproben nicht aus?
Die Idee stammt ursprünglich von einer Gruppe Landwirten in Kanada, die dies zum Spaß mit Unterhosen aus dem eigenen Schrank durchgeführt hatten. Wir hatten die Idee zunächst für eine kleine Aktion übernommen, um Familien und Kinder auf Böden als lebendiges System aufmerksam zu machen. Nachdem diese kleine Aktion viel Medienaufmerksamkeit erhielt, kam die Idee auf, daraus ein größeres Projekt zu starten und dabei wissenschaftlich zu testen, was genau Unterhosen uns über unsere Böden sagen können.
Für Bodenproben entnimmt man etwas Boden und analysiert dann chemische und physikalische Eigenschaften. Bodenprozesse kann man damit nicht gut abbilden. Die Unterhosen sind im Feld und zeigen direkt, was die Bodenlebewesen dort vor Ort machen. Außerdem zeigen sie eindrücklich, dass der Boden lebt. Bei vielen ist der Moment, bei dem sie die Unterhose wieder ausgraben wirklich ein „Aha“-Moment. Man kann direkt erleben und fühlen, was dort im Boden alles los ist. Eine solche Erfahrung kann keine Laboranalyse bieten.
Uni Zürich setzt auf Citizen Science und erhält große Unterstützung
Neben 2.000 Unterhosen, haben Sie auch 12.000 Teebeutel vergraben lassen. Dazu benötigten Sie Hilfe aus der Bevölkerung. Wie haben Sie die Menschen erreicht?
Das ging überraschend einfach. Wir haben Aufrufe zur Teilnahme in landwirtschaftlichen und anderen Zeitschriften und Newslettern veröffentlicht. Wir haben auch gezielt mit Social Media nach Teilnehmenden gesucht. Wir haben allen Teilnehmenden eine umfassende Laboranalyse mit detaillierten Erklärungen und Interpretationshilfen versprochen. Am Ende mussten wir 400 Menschen wieder absagen, weil es unsere Kapazitäten überstieg.
Welche Maßgaben mussten die Freiwilligen beim Vergraben der Unterhosen und Teebeutel erfüllen?
Wir haben allen Teilnehmenden ein Paket mit neuen Baumwollunterhosen, sowie Teebeuteln zusammen mit detaillierten Anleitungen zukommen lassen. Es war wichtig, dass alles möglichst in einem standardisierten Verfahren vergraben wurde, damit es auch wissenschaftlich vergleichbar und auswertbar ist. Außerdem haben die Teilnehmenden Bodenproben entnommen. Nachdem alle Unterhosen und Teebeutel wieder ausgegraben waren, schickten sie uns alles wieder zurück ins Labor zur Analyse. Zudem hatten wir eine Smartphone-App, in der Teilnehmende Hintergrundinformationen zur Fläche, wo vergraben wurde, und zur Bewirtschaftung eingeben konnten. Dort könnten sie auch Fotos machen und alles auf eine Karte hochladen. Dort kann man immer noch sehen, wo überall Unterhosen vergraben wurden.
Hilfe von Freiwilligen und Laborarbeiter:innen im Akkord
Nach zwei Monaten kamen die Unterhosen und Teebeutel zurück ins Labor. Wie ging es da weiter?
Die Teebeutel wurden von Bodenresten befreit und gewogen, um den Abbau abzuschätzen. Auch die Unterhosen wurden gereinigt und gewogen. Da dies jedoch nicht allzu exakte Daten lieferte – es blieb immer etwas Boden hängen, was das Gewicht beeinflusst – haben wir sie dann digital fotografiert und den Verlust an Pixeln im Vergleich zu einer neuen Unterhose als Maß für den Abbau genommen. Insgesamt haben wir über ein Jahr gebraucht, um alle grob 8000 Teebeutel und 1750 Unterhosen, die wir zurückerhalten hatten, zu analysieren. Außerdem hat unser Bodenlabor Marathonarbeit geleistet und knapp 900 Bodenproben auf Kohlenstoffgehalt, pH-Wert, Nährstoffkonzentrationen, Textur und weiteres analysiert.
Ließ sich auf der Basis der Überreste der Unterhosen eine Art Typologie erstellen? Beispielsweise: Waren nur noch die Nähte und der Bund erhalten, fällt das in die Kategorie „gute Bodenqualität“?
Das war unsere ursprüngliche Hypothese: Viel Abbau – gesunder Boden, wenig Abbau – schlechter Boden. Doch, wie so oft im Boden, gibt es keine einfache Antwort. Über alle Standorte hinweg konnten wir zwar diesen Trend erkennen, aber die Variation war sehr groß. Wir haben gesehen, dass der Unterhosenabbau mit der Nährstoffverfügbarkeit im Boden zusammenhing. Je mehr Nährstoffe, desto größer der Abbau. Doch teilweise waren die Nährstoffkonzentrationen im Boden, besonders in Privatgärten, auch extrem hoch.
Doch die Unterhosen können trotzdem sehr interessant sein und informative Einblicke in den Boden geben, wenn man dazu noch andere Faktoren mit einbezieht. Ist der Boden feucht – nicht zu nass und nicht zu trocken – und die Temperatur einigermassen warm, erwartet man einen hohen Unterhosenabbau. Ist dies nicht der Fall, kann es sein, dass man ein Problem mit der Bodenstruktur hat, zum Beispiel Verdichtung, oder, dass der Boden sehr nährstoffarm ist. Dann könnte man das gezielt prüfen. Ist andererseits der Abbau sehr hoch, sollte man testen, ob man nicht etwas zu viel düngt. Das Vergraben einer Unterhose kann viel über den Boden aussagen und zum Nachdenken anregen. Es hilft sicherlich dabei, Bodenprozesses besser zu verstehen und durch genaues Beobachten kann man viel lernen.
Nächste Citizen-Science-Projekte stehen an
Sie schreiben, dass sich die Unterhosen am meisten in Privatgärten zersetzten, mittlere Zersetzung auf Äckern und Wiesen und Rasenfläche die geringste biologische Aktivität zeigte. Waren Sie von den Ergebnissen überrascht?
Ein wenig schon. Unter Wiesen findet man in der Regel reichhaltige und aktive Bodengemeinschaften und dort hätte ich die stärksten Effekte erwartet, der Abbau war aber nur mittelmäßig. Im Nachhinein macht es aber total Sinn. In Privatgärten wird oft Kompost eingesetzt, es wird bewässert. Dies sind Bedingungen, in denen Bodenlebewesen sehr aktiv sein können, weil sie viele Ressourcen finden. Rasenflächen sind oft Monokulturen, teilweise mit Herbiziden behandelt. Der geringe Abbau ist also auch nicht überraschend.
Hatten Sie selbst auch Unterhosen und/oder Teebeutel in Ihrem Garten vergraben?
Ja, gemeinsam mit meiner Tochter haben wir natürlich auch selbst Unterhosen vergaben.
Können die Menschen weiterhin bei dem Projekt mitmachen – nicht nur in der Schweiz offenbar? Ich habe gesehen, dass es auch Karten-Einträge bei München gab.
Ja, die App steht für alle Interessierten zur Verfügung. Wir haben sie erweitert und insgesamt acht Methoden eingebaut, mit denen jede/r seinen/Ihren Boden untersuchen und kennenlernen kann, auch ohne Labor. Momentan arbeiten wir noch daran, das Ganze nutzerfreundlicher zu gestalten und wir überarbeiten die Anleitungen. Die App kann im Prinzip von Überall genutzt werden.
Haben Sie schon eine Idee für ein neues Citizen-Science-Projekt?
Ja, wir starten gerade das Projekt Soil Bodies – The living Tapestry, wo wir das Verhältnis der Modeindustrie und Boden beleuchten wollen. Dabei sollen alte Kleidungsstücke vergraben werden. Wir schauen dann, wie sich unterschiedliche Materialien abbauen, oder auch nicht. Mit unserer App kann dabei auch der Boden untersucht werden. Aus den abgebauten Kleidungsstücken erstellen wir am Ende die „Living Tapestry“ (dt.: der lebendige Wandteppich), ein großes Kunstwerk. Aus einem Teil des Kunstwerks wird eine Modekollektion entstehen. Alle Interessierten können teilnehmen.

articles.title: 3 razones para ver 'Susurran tu nombre', la nueva película de Robert De Niro que triunfa en Netflix
articles.text:
Netflix acaba de estrenar hace unos días la película Susurran tu nombre. Y su llegada a la plataforma no podía haber sido mejor. Desde que viera la luz, se ha situado como la número 1 en el ranking de películas más vistas de todo su catálogo. Un ejemplo perfecto de cómo, sin necesidad de hacer demasiado ruido, los suscriptores sí responden a las propuestas que el servicio de streaming les lanza cuando estas son lo suficientemente atractivas.
Según FlixPatrol, Susurran tu nombre es la película más vista de la semana en Netflix en todo el mundo. Es cierto que la recepción tanto de la crítica profesional como del público general ha sido mixta. Pero sí que cuenta con ciertos elementos destacables que la hacen lo suficientemente interesante como para darle una oportunidad.
Susurran tu nombre se estrenó en Netflix el pasado 28 de agosto, pero ha conseguido mantenerse en lo más alto durante todo este tiempo. El filme es obra del director James Ashcroft bajo el guion de Ben Jacoby y Chase Palmer. La historia está basada en la novela de Alex North.
El drama familiar
Aunque la historia trata sobre una misteriosa desaparición y su consecuente investigación detectivesca, hay un halo que lo envuelve todo: el drama de una familia rota. Para empezar, el protagonista es un padre que ve cómo su hijo pequeño ha desaparecido. Un claro simbolismo de la distancia que se crea en demasiadas ocasiones entre padres e hijos. Y, para colmo, el hombre debe recurrir a su padre, al que no ve desde hace 25 años y con quien no tiene ningún tipo de relación. La temática de las relaciones rotas paternofiliales está presente de principio a fin, dotando a Susurran tu nombre de un tono muy distintivo.
El thriller de misterio
El hilo conductor que mueve Susurran tu nombre es en realidad un misterio que se antoja como un clásico thriller criminal y de suspense. Y es que la trama de la película reza lo siguiente. Cuando secuestran a un niño de 8 años, su padre viudo, un escritor de novelas policíacas, recurre a su propio padre en busca de ayuda. Y es que este anciano es en realidad un antiguo detective de policía jubilado. Al reencontrarse, descubrirán una conexión con un caso de hace décadas sobre un asesino en serie conocido como «El Hombre Susurrante»". A lo largo del filme, los protagonistas y los espectadores deberán descubrir la identidad del secuestrador y encontrar al hijo de Jake.
Un reparto de lujo
Aunque sí hay una razón para ver Susurran tu nombre en Netflix, esa es su reparto. Muy pocas películas pueden presumir de un elenco como este. A la cabeza, el legendario Robert De Niro, ganador de dos premios Óscar y uno de los mejores actores de la historia de Hollywood. Junto a él, como su hijo, está Adam Scott, el protagonista de la exitosa serie Severance. Además, la cinta cuenta con otros nombres tan importantes como Michelle Monaghan o Michael Keaton.

articles.title: The Hidden Financial Challenges of Scaling an Ecommerce Business - Tech Guide
articles.text:
Growing an ecommerce business can look straightforward from the outside: more customers arrive, order volumes increase, and revenue moves in the right direction.
Behind that growth, however, financial responsibilities often become considerably more complicated, especially when a business begins selling across multiple states and managing different compliance obligations. Working with an Online sales tax consultant can help ecommerce businesses understand services related to sales tax registration, filing, exemptions, and ongoing compliance as their operations expand across the United States.
Revenue Growth Does Not Always Mean Stronger Cash Flow
A rising sales figure can create the impression that a business has more money available to invest, but revenue and cash flow tell very different stories. Growing companies frequently need to purchase larger quantities of inventory, increase advertising budgets, hire additional support, and upgrade technology before the resulting revenue reaches the bank. This timing difference can leave a successful ecommerce company surprisingly short of accessible cash.
Payment processing schedules can make the situation even more complicated because funds are not always available immediately after a sale. Refunds, chargebacks, supplier deposits, shipping expenses, and marketplace fees can also reduce the amount of usable cash generated from each transaction. Leaders therefore need to monitor cash movement carefully rather than treating sales growth as proof of financial strength.
Inventory Becomes a Bigger Financial Commitment
Inventory is often one of the largest expenses facing a growing ecommerce operation. When demand increases, businesses may order additional stock to prevent popular products from selling out, but forecasting future demand becomes harder as product ranges and customer numbers expand. Ordering too much can leave valuable capital sitting in warehouses instead of being used elsewhere in the company.
Ordering too little creates a different financial problem because stock shortages can result in missed sales and frustrated customers. Seasonal demand, supplier delays, changing consumer preferences, and minimum order requirements all make inventory planning more difficult at scale. Effective forecasting becomes essential for maintaining a balance between product availability and healthy cash reserves.
Compliance Gets More Complicated With Expansion
Selling to customers across the United States can expose an ecommerce company to financial obligations that were less important during its early stages. Sales tax requirements can vary between states, and growth may eventually create responsibilities that the business did not previously have. Companies need reliable systems for identifying where obligations exist and keeping the appropriate records.
The administrative burden can also increase as sales channels multiply. A business selling through its own website and several marketplaces may have transaction information spread across different platforms, making accurate reporting more difficult. Addressing these processes early can help prevent compliance responsibilities from becoming a disruptive financial problem later.
Customer Acquisition Can Become More Expensive
Marketing is another area where growth can introduce hidden costs. A campaign that performed well when a business was small may become less efficient as the company attempts to reach larger audiences, enter new markets, or compete for increasingly expensive advertising placements. Maintaining the same rate of growth can therefore require progressively larger marketing budgets.
Business leaders should pay attention to profitability at the customer level rather than focusing exclusively on traffic, orders, or revenue. Customer acquisition costs need to be considered alongside average order values, repeat purchases, returns, discounts, and fulfillment expenses. Without this broader view, a company can generate impressive sales numbers while earning very little from each new customer.
Returns and Fulfillment Can Reduce Margins
Shipping and fulfillment expenses can rise quickly as order volumes increase. Businesses may need additional warehouse space, more packaging materials, fulfillment partners, international shipping services, or faster delivery options to meet customer expectations. These costs can quietly reduce margins if pricing strategies are not adjusted as operations become more sophisticated.
Returns create another layer of expense because the cost extends beyond simply refunding the customer. Companies may pay for return shipping, inspection, repackaging, customer support, and inventory processing, while some returned products cannot be resold at their original price. Tracking the true cost of returns helps leaders identify products or processes that are putting unnecessary pressure on profitability.
Technology and Staffing Require Continued Investment
Small ecommerce businesses can often operate with relatively simple software and a compact team, but those arrangements may not survive rapid growth. Higher transaction volumes can require better accounting tools, inventory management systems, customer service platforms, security solutions, and automation. Subscription costs that once seemed minor can become substantial when several systems are needed simultaneously.
Staffing expenses can increase just as quickly. Customer service, finance, marketing, logistics, technology, and compliance responsibilities eventually become too demanding for a founder or small team to handle effectively. Hiring strategically and automating repetitive processes can help a company increase capacity without allowing overhead to grow faster than revenue.
Protecting Profitability While the Business Grows
Scaling successfully requires leaders to look beyond headline revenue and understand what growth actually costs. Cash flow, inventory, compliance, marketing, fulfillment, technology, and staffing are interconnected, meaning pressure in one area can quickly affect another. Regular financial forecasting can help decision makers identify these pressures before they become serious obstacles.
Growth should also be measured by the quality of revenue rather than its volume alone. A smaller increase in sales accompanied by healthy margins and predictable cash flow may be more valuable than rapid expansion supported by excessive spending. Sustainable ecommerce businesses are built by leaders who understand when to invest aggressively and when financial discipline should take priority.
Conclusion
Scaling an ecommerce business creates opportunities that can transform a small operation into a significant company, but growth introduces financial challenges that are easy to underestimate. Rising inventory commitments, complicated compliance requirements, marketing expenses, fulfillment costs, technology investments, and staffing needs can all reduce the financial benefits of increasing sales. Leaders who monitor these hidden costs, strengthen their financial systems, and prepare for new responsibilities can pursue growth without sacrificing the stability that made expansion possible in the first place.

articles.title: China’s AI labs siphoned Claude’s intelligence?
articles.text:
China’s AI labs siphoned Claude’s intelligence?
Anthropic’s report reveals that major Chinese AI developers operated illicit proxy networks to harvest Claude’s reasoning capabilities, unintentionally leaking sensitive military, government, and corporate secrets in the process.
Dear Reader,
Anthropic’s latest report alleges that seven Chinese AI labs used fraudulent accounts, proxy networks, and other techniques to extract capabilities from its Claude models. Alibaba reportedly generated over 151 million exchanges to train Qwen, while Moonshot AI and DeepSeek allegedly routed millions of user queries to Claude, exposing sensitive government, military and corporate data to US servers.
Meanwhile, OpenAI has temporarily paused new subscriptions to its $200-a-month Pro plan after demand for its newly-launched Astra AI model exceeded the company’s expectations. The surge in usage has reportedly put pressure on OpenAI’s computing capacity, prompting it to limit new Pro sign-ups while it works to accommodate demand. Astra, launched earlier this month, is available across OpenAI’s paid plans and is positioned as a more capable model for tasks including coding and computer use.
On the domestic front, Hero Motors is set to launch its Rs 1,000 crore IPO next week, with the two-wheeler components maker looking to raise fresh capital as well as provide an exit to existing shareholders.
In other news, California has approved new rules restricting how social media platforms can engage users under 16, including curbs on features such as infinite scroll and autoplay. The package also introduces tighter safeguards for AI chatbots and bans AI companion chatbot toys for four years, as the state steps up efforts to protect children online.
In today’s newsletter, we will talk about
- Anthropic report flags offline execution risks
- Desi Tales bets on comfy festive kidswear
Here’s your trivia for today: What streaming media device and platform was originally developed as an internal project at Netflix before spinning off in 2008? (Scroll down for the answer)
News
Anthropic report flags offline execution risks
In its September 2026 Threat Intelligence Report, Anthropic highlighted a critical structural vulnerability in current AI safety frameworks. While suspending or banning cloud accounts remains the primary defense for AI providers, it is becoming an incomplete remedy. The report reveals that once an AI model generates offline software, firmware, or standalone execution scripts, these digital artifacts continue to operate in the physical world completely beyond the reach of cloud-level bans or provider interventions.
Key takeaways:
- Compiled software—like Russian drone swarm scripts, Yemeni missile tools, and Malian surveillance code—continues operating locally in physical systems long after developers' cloud accounts are blocked.
- Threat actors use agentic AI frameworks that automatically rewrite and recompile blocked malware code on the fly to continually bypass detection systems.
- Advanced AI coding capabilities enable single, low-resourced operators to run complex, state-grade cyberattacks and hardware exploits previously requiring whole organisations.

Round: Undisclosed
Startup: Graph AI
Amount: $13.3M
Round: Series A

Desi Tales bets on comfy festive kidswear
What started as a weekend venture in Bengaluru is now a bootstrapped kidswear brand building a business around traditional Indian clothing. Desi Tales is targeting parents looking for festive outfits that balance contemporary styles with traditional craft. The brand is now looking to widen its reach as demand for children’s ethnic wear grows.
Key takeaways:
- Desi Tales makes 100% cotton ethnic wear, nightwear, and co-ord sets, priced between Rs 599 and Rs 1,799.
- The brand has served nearly 40,000 customers and says revenue has grown about 30% annually, without external funding.
- Desi Tales plans to expand to online marketplaces, invest in performance marketing and open two more retail outlets.

articles.title: Voiture offerte en cas d'incendie et batterie garantie à vie : le pari fou de Xiaomi
articles.text:
Pour s’imposer en tant qu’outsider, il faut redoubler d’imagination. Souvenez-vous de la garantie 7 ans déployée par Kia sur sa Cee’d, une première qui a marqué les esprits ! 20 ans plus tard, c’est au tour des Chinois de séduire pour espérer pénétrer le marché. Et l’argument prix ne suffit plus pour faire signer le bon de commande. Xiaomi ressort donc un atout clé : une garantie massue autrement plus impressionnante que celle de Kia.
La marque chinoise garantit en effet sa nouvelle batterie Dragonscale à vie contre la combustion spontanée et les incendies survenant après un accident. Autant dire que si ça flambe pour une raison X ou Y, vous êtes normalement couvert ! Développée en partenariat avec CALB et Sunwoda, cet accumulateur prometteur dépasserait largement les normes chinoises en matière de sécurité.
Garantie à vie et voiture offerte : que cache cette offre folle ?
Li Xiaoshuang, vice-PDG de la branche automobile de Xiaomi, explique que cette prouesse a été possible par une sélection rigoureuse des matières premières combinées à une conception et une fabrication au centre de toutes les attentions. Cela permet ainsi à la marque d’être extrêmement confiante sur ses batteries en offrant carrément un nouveau véhicule en cas d’incendie dû à un défaut de fabrication.
Dans le cas d’un accident, Xiaomi prendra en charge la différence entre l’indemnisation de l’assurance et la valeur du véhicule estimée avant la collision. Il faut dire que la batterie Dragonscale possède des isolateurs haute tension avec des temps de commutation de quelques millisecondes permettant de réagir au plus vite en cas d’anomalie. Des matériaux ultra isolants englobent le tout pour éviter toute transmission de chaleur excessive.
Une protection survitaminée grâce à l’intelligence artificielle
Les cellules sont d’autre part constamment surveillées grâce à une IA basée sur le cloud. Xiaomi ajoute que ce système contrôle leur état dix fois plus fréquemment que ne l’exigent les normes locales. Ainsi, lors de tests grandeur nature menés à 55°C, les cellules isolées en feu ne peuvent provoquer un incendie généralisé de la batterie. Cet argument clé aura de quoi rassurer les sceptiques toujours effrayés par les explosions de modèles électriques.
Cela dit, il y a une poignée d’exclusions comme pour toute garantie qui se respecte. Seuls les véhicules de première main vendus aux particuliers sont éligibles à la mesure. Les véhicules utilisés professionnellement par les taxis ne sont pas concernés, tout comme les modèles d’occasion. Un entretien régulier du véhicule dans les centres agréés Xiaomi est également attendu. En Chine, la batterie Dragonscale équipe les SUV Skynomad N70 et N90.

articles.title: ICYMI: the 7 biggest tech stories of the week, from Apple's iPhone Duo debut to Sonos' best compact speaker yet
articles.text:
ICYMI: the 7 biggest tech stories of the week, from Apple's iPhone Duo debut to Sonos' best compact speaker yet
Your firmware update for September 12, 2026
This week, Apple announced its iPhone 18 Pro and something entirely new: the first iPhone foldable in the incredible iPhone Duo.
There was plenty more to catch up on this week, including not one but two Nintendo Directs, and an LG privacy scandal.
To catch up on all this and more, scroll down. But before you read about the news, you might want to try your hand at our quiz on the biggest events of the week.
7. LG TVs were in the privacy doghouse again
LG isn’t exactly a stranger to privacy storms, and it found itself in the middle of another big one this week thanks to a new report that made some big accusations about its TVs.
An investigation by Gamers Nexus and independent security researchers claimed that LG TVs can capture audio even when the screens are off and also monitor your entire home. These findings didn’t exactly sit well with clips of LG executives pitching to advertisers by saying “we own the glass” in reference to its TVs.
LG hit back at the claims, telling us in a statement that “the claims made in the recently published video are not true”. Still, the accusations may leave a bad taste for some, particularly as they come a month after claims (also refuted by LG) that its monitors were installing adware on PCs.
- Read the full story: 'It's extremely creepy': LG TVs collect far more data on you than you'd expect, says new report — but LG hits back, saying the claims made 'are not true'
6. A new ‘brain wearable’ arrived to track our stress
What if you could track your brain and thoughts in the same way that fitness trackers log your heart rate? That’s what a new wave of wearables is promising — and another ‘brain pattern monitor’ arrived this week, before quickly selling out its first batch.
Sign up for breaking news, reviews, opinion, top tech deals, and more.
The Atlas 1.0 sits behind your ear and tracks things like your attention span, stress levels and energy burn. In theory, the benefit of understanding these brain patterns is that the Atlas can then connect them to certain triggers — for example, revealing that social media is actually stressing you out rather than relaxing you.
We haven’t tried out this particular brain wearable yet, but our Senior Fitness & Wearables Editor Matt Evans did electrocute his own vagus nerve for a week with Nurosym’s gadget, so we’d certainly be up for the challenge when the Atlas 1.0 is back in stock.
- Read the full story: The Atlas 1.0 Pioneer Edition is a $499 brain scanner that sits behind your ear to measure your stress, attention span and energy — and the first batch has just sold out
5. Sonos debuted an Ultra soundbar
Matt Bolton got to hear the new and upgraded Sonos Beam Ultra soundbar, which sits above the Sonos Beam (Gen 2) in Sonos’ range, but is more affordable than the Sonos Arc Ultra. It promises a 7.1.2 Dolby Atmos sound system from nine built-in speakers, including two upfiring speakers, that’s much bigger, wider and more immersive than Sonos’ existing small soundbar… and based on Matt’s experience so far, it comfortably delivers.
Matt said the way the sound is disconnected from the soundbar is seriously impressive for such a compact box, with sound effects coming from way over at the sides of the room, and voices coming through really clearly, and emanating from the screen, not the box. The bass handling was great as well, despite the lack of a dedicated sub. Is this now the ultimate small soundbar option?
- Read the full story: I heard the Sonos Beam Ultra, and it delivers the most impressive Dolby Atmos sound I've experienced from a compact soundbar
4. Nintendo doubled up Directs
Nintendo treated us to not one, but two Direct livestreams this week — and both caused quite a stir.
The first was devoted to the Legend of Zelda series’s 40th anniversary and gave us our first real look at the upcoming Ocarina of Time remake. Unfortunately, its visuals were immediately divisive, with some online commenters comparing the more “realistic” direction to Nvidia’s widely mocked DLSS 5.
On a more positive note, a new Nintendo Switch 2 model inspired by the franchise was also revealed, and it already seems like it’s going to be a big hit with pre-orders flying off digital shelves.
The second Direct came one day later and focused on more general Switch and Switch 2 software news. Major announcements included the reveal of a new Metroid game, tantalizingly titled Metroid Ravenous, and free updates for Star Fox and Mario Kart World that introduce new content delighting fans.
- Read the full story: Everything announced at Nintendo Direct — from a new 2D Metroid game to a surprise Mario Kart World update, and massive Kirby reveal
3. Apple announced more than iPhones
Apple’s iPhones may have taken center stage, but some other gadgets also featured in its showcase: two new Apple Watches and the AirPods 5.
Apple’s earbuds were a fairly standard affair. The company promises better noise cancellation, a more comfortable fit, and the premium pair that comes with a wireless charging case also boasts on-AirPods volume controls — because, of course, a standard feature on other wireless earbuds is sold at a markup.
As for the Watches (Series 12 and Ultra 4), any upgrades were overshadowed by some new Siri tools. Conversation rewind will let you read a recap of the last 15 seconds of conversation, and it’s being billed as useful accessibility for folks who are hard of hearing. Meanwhile, Siri Recaps will see your Watch listen in on your day’s conversations to create a recap at the very end of the key details you heard in a quick summary. Apple has promised there are plenty of privacy protections, and that no recordings are stored, but it has some worried the ongoing wearable privacy debate is going in the wrong direction.
Read the full story: Thanks to Siri Recaps, your Apple Watch is always listening as you go about your day
2. Apple’s iPhone 18 Pro landed
The iPhone 18 Pro boasts many of the expected changes we’ve come to expect: an improved (A20 Pro) chipset, enhanced AI capabilities, a longer 36-hour battery life, and a few new color options (Silver returns, but it also comes in Black, Glacier, and Burgundy).
Our favorite new feature, however, is the arrival of variable aperture. Most phones boast a set aperture size, which determines how much light the lens can receive, and it usually has to compromise between maximizing nighttime quality (which wants a more open aperture) and depth of field (which wants a more closed aperture). Software trickery can help, but Apple’s mechanical approach means your iPhone 18 Pro can automatically swap to the setting that’s best for the current conditions and your photo needs — and pros can also manually control the setting if they want.
As expected based on leaks, but perhaps surprising to the non-Apple-obsessed, there was no iPhone 18. Instead, all of Apple’s older iPhone 17-series devices got a price hike.
- Read the full story: I just tried the iPhone 18 Pro — and Apple gave me two surprisingly good reasons to upgrade
1. We unfolded the iPhone Duo
Let’s round things off with a tech story you definitely didn’t miss this week: the debut of Apple’s first foldable iPhone, the iPhone Duo.
Originally thought to be called the iPhone Ultra, the Duo boasts a similar passport-style shape to the Samsung Galaxy Z Fold 8, but it’s a distinct foldable product in a few key ways. Two of its corners are rounded, meaning the phone’s 7.6-inch inner screen unfolds into an almost iPad mini-like shape; Apple opted to use Touch ID rather than Face ID, so there’s no visible inner-display camera; it sports a Galaxy-beating IP68 durability rating; and there’s a gorgeous open and close animation that passes across the screen when you’re switching between folded and unfolded states.
Of course, there are question marks. The Duo only packs two rear cameras; it’s both thicker and heavier than the Z Fold 8; and, of course, it’s the most expensive iPhone ever released. But, in recent memory, it’s hard to think of a more hype-inducing consumer tech product than this. We’ve been hands-on with the iPhone Duo, and our full review is coming soon.

articles.title: Es el reloj más potente de Apple (y el más caro): todo lo que cambia del Watch Ultra 4 frente al Ultra 3
articles.text:
Cuando Apple lanza nuevos dispositivos, no siempre es sencillo ver dónde están los cambios más importantes. Ya os los hemos contado sobre los iPhone Pro y Pro Max, incluso del Apple Watch Series 12. En esta ocasión nos vamos a centrar en el nuevo reloj tope de gama de la compañía: vamos a ver las principales diferencias entre el Apple Watch Ultra 4 y su antecesor.
Apple Watch Ultra 4 GPS + Cellular con Caja de Titanio Negro de 49 mm
Estas son las principales diferencias entre el Apple Watch Ultra 4 y el Watch Ultra 3
Nuevo chip S11
Por fuera, el nuevo Ultra de Apple es idéntico al anterior modelo. Las novedades del Watch Ultra 4 llegan en su interior, empezando por un nuevo procesador: el chip S11. Este, que también está presente en el Apple Watch Series 12, promete un mejor rendimiento y mayor eficiencia, lo que repercutirá en la autonomía. Sin embargo, lo verdaderamente importante del mismo es que es la base de varias novedades en materia de IA que agrega este nuevo reloj.
Un nuevo arsenal de herramientas de inteligencia artificial
A nivel de software, una de las principales novedades de este nuevo Ultra se llama Audio Intelligence. Se trata de una categoría de funciones de inteligencia artificial donde destacan varias, como Siri Recap, que analizará nuestras conversaciones y nos dará un breve resumen sobre ellas. Apple explica que estas no se almacenarán ni se generará una transcripción automática de ellas, pretendiendo así diferenciarse de otros dispositivos. El dispositivo también omitirá datos sensibles a la hora del resumen.
Junto a esta, también está otra función llamada Live Rewind, la cual nos permitirá recuperar los últimos 15 segundos de una conversación en formato de texto. También llega una función de accesibilidad para personas con problemas auditivos que avisará al usuario si detecta sonidos como sirenas o el llanto de un bebé, todo sin la necesidad de tener el móvil cerca.
Todo esto pinta genial, pero hay un pequeño “pero”: en Europa, no recibiremos nada de esto hasta el próximo año.
También llegan mejoras en materia de salud
Otra de las principales novedades del Ultra la tenemos en materia de salud. Este nuevo reloj de Apple estrena un sensor de ritmo cardiaco que mide de forma continua las 24 horas del día. Se trata de un cambio importante con respecto a relojes anteriores de la compañía, puesto que estos solo registraban el ritmo cardiaco de forma continua durante el ejercicio (durante el resto del día, a intervalos).
Además, llega una herramienta nueva que se llama Disposición. Esta, en esencia, va analizando nuestra actividad diaria continuamente con datos sobre el ejercicio, las constantes vitales o la calidad del sueño. Con toda esa información, el sistema irá dándonos indicaciones para afrontar el día para decirnos si estamos preparados o conviene tomarse las cosas con más calma.
Hay mejora en la autonomía
Apple no da especificaciones concretas sobre la capacidad de la batería de sus dispositivos, pero parece que la llegada del nuevo procesador hace que este Apple Watch Ultra 4 ofrezca mejor autonomía. En modo ahorro, el nuevo reloj puede llegar hasta las 50 horas de autonomía, lo que supone una mejora con respecto a las 42 horas de autonomía en el mismo modo del Apple Watch Ultra 3.
Otra mejora la tenemos en la carga, especialmente para esas veces que tenemos poco tiempo para ello. Apple promete que, cargando 15 minutos el nuevo Watch Ultra 4, tendremos 18 horas de autonomía, una mejora bastante notable frente al modelo anterior (que ofrecía 12 horas).
Los precios
Toca hablar del precio y, en este caso, no hay diferencia (aunque con matices). El Apple Watch Ultra 4 llega a un precio de 899 euros en su versión más económica, el mismo PVP que tiene el Apple Watch Ultra 3. ¿Qué ocurre? Que el modelo anterior, al ya llevar un tiempo en el mercado, hace que sea más fácil encontrarlo a mejor precio. Sin ir más lejos, ahora mismo está disponible por 799 euros.
¿Qué Apple Watch Ultra elegir?
Por qué elegir el Apple Watch Ultra 3
Ya no es el más moderno, pero el Apple Watch Ultra 3 es una opción bastante interesante en 2026:
- Su precio es menor: Al llevar más tiempo en tiendas, es más sencillo encontrarlo a un menor precio. Ahora mismo hay 100 euros de diferencia con respecto al nuevo modelo.
- El nuevo modelo trae novedades, pero no demasiadas: El nuevo procesador y las funciones que agrega el Ultra 4 pueden no ser suficientes como para justificar pagar la diferencia. Además, algunas novedades no las podremos disfrutar hasta que lleguen a Europa.
Apple Watch Ultra 3 GPS + Cellular, Reloj prémium para Running y Multideporte con Caja de Titanio Resistente de 49 mm y Correa Ocean Azul náutico. Monitores avanzados de Salud
Por qué elegir el Apple Watch Ultra 4
El Apple Watch Ultra llega con un nuevo procesador y varias mejoras interesantes. Esto son sus puntos clave:
- Nuevo procesador: Su procesador S11 es la base para las novedades en IA que llegarán el año que viene y aporta un extra de rendimiento.
- Más autonomía: Según promete Apple, el nuevo modelo ofrece 8 horas más de autonomía.
- La medición cardiaca continua: A nivel de salud, la medición cardiaca continua es una de las novedades más destacadas y puede ser un motivo de compra si lo necesitas.

articles.title: Diablo V, StarCraft en monde ouvert, Switch 2 : Blizzard dévoile ses plans jusqu'en 2030
articles.text:
La grand-messe de Blizzard a repris ses droits ce week-end. Lors de la cérémonie d’ouverture de la BlizzCon 2026, ce samedi 12 septembre, l’éditeur a enchaîné les révélations, que l’on a suivies en direct. On vous résume l’essentiel, une annonce à la fois.
StarCraft renaît, en jeu de tir en monde ouvert
La vraie surprise vient de là. Seize ans après StarCraft II, Blizzard ressuscite sa saga de science-fiction, mais délaisse la stratégie en temps réel qui a fait sa gloire au profit d’un jeu de tir (shooter) en monde ouvert, sobrement intitulé StarCraft et attendu au printemps 2030. Direction, à nouveau, le secteur Koprulu.
Le projet est confié à Dan Hay, un vétéran de la saga Far Cry passé par Ubisoft : un profil de gros jeu d’action à monde ouvert, donc. Cette licence de stratégie phare des années 2000 n’avait plus reçu le moindre contenu solo depuis Nova Covert Ops, en 2016.
Or un jeu de tir dans cet univers, ça réveille surtout le souvenir de StarCraft : Ghost, ce projet de shooter jamais sorti, annulé après des années de développement. Blizzard, qui n’a dévoilé qu’une cinématique de présentation, n’avait plus sorti pareil lapin de son chapeau depuis la BlizzCon 2019.
Diablo V arrive au printemps 2029
Diablo V est l’autre gros morceau. Officiellement en développement, la suite de la saga vise un lancement au printemps 2029.
Le postulat a de quoi dérouter les habitués du hack’n’slash (ces jeux d’action où l’on taille dans des hordes de démons pour ramasser du butin) : pour la première fois, on incarne des héros dans un Sanctuaire où le Mal a déjà gagné et où les champions ont été vaincus.
Sanctuaire est tombé, Diablo a triomphé, résume l’écran-titre. Blizzard pose même la question qui structure le jeu, celle de savoir ce que l’on doit devenir quand le monde s’est déjà effondré. Le studio n’a pour l’instant montré qu’un premier aperçu, sans gameplay ni date précise, comme le détaille son récapitulatif officiel.
Une série animée Diablo en chantier chez Netflix
Blizzard élargit ses univers au-delà du jeu, et l’a dit : le nom du studio est Blizzard Entertainment, et non pas Blizzard Games.
Une série animée située dans le monde de Diablo est en développement avec Netflix, comme l’a relayé le compte officiel de la licence. Peu de détails pour l’instant, si ce n’est que l’éditeur présente ça comme un point de départ : il laisse entendre que d’autres adaptations se préparent autour de ses franchises.
Le studio suit un chemin déjà tracé par ses voisins, entre l’univers d’Arcane tiré de League of Legends et l’adaptation de The Last of Us, où le jeu vidéo nourrit désormais séries et films.
World of Warcraft : Forever, un nouveau WoW permanent
World of Warcraft accueille une troisième version permanente, à côté du WoW moderne et de WoW Classic. Baptisée World of Warcraft : Forever, elle se veut un Azeroth « familier mais neuf », centré sur le monde, la communauté et le voyage plutôt que sur la course effrénée au contenu de fin de partie.
L’aventure se déroule après les événements de Warcraft III Reforged : Forsaken Kingdom et avant Molten Core (Le Cœur du Magma, qui est un des premiers raids), avec un retour sur les continents d’origine, une montée jusqu’au niveau 60, puis de nouvelles histoires et mises à jour au fil du temps.
Le lancement est fixé au 4 novembre, avec une bêta qui démarre le 17 septembre. La cinématique d’annonce et un extrait de gameplay ont été dévoilés dans la foulée.
Diablo IV débarque sur Nintendo Switch 2
Annonce plus terre à terre pour clore le tour : Diablo IV arrive sur Nintendo Switch 2 le 15 septembre. Une fuite l’avait déjà éventée cet été, la voilà officielle.
Le portage prend la forme d’une Diablo IV : Age of Hatred Collection, qui regroupe le jeu de base et ses deux extensions, Vessel of Hatred et Lord of Hatred. De quoi arpenter les jungles de Nahantu et les rivages de Skovos, Joy-Con 2 en main.
En une conférence, Blizzard a donc balisé ses cinq prochaines années : un WoW jouable presque tout de suite, deux gros jeux à l’horizon 2029-2030, une incursion chez Netflix et un portage console.
Pour un studio qui sortait d’années compliquées, entre polémiques internes et rachat par Microsoft en octobre 2023, la feuille de route a au moins le mérite d’être lisible. Un printemps 2030 pour StarCraft, en revanche, c’est encore très loin.

articles.title: French Days : le Roborock Qrevo Edge 2 tombe à 589,98€ chez Amazon
articles.text:
Les French Days font redescendre le Roborock Qrevo Edge 2 à 589,98 € chez Amazon, contre 889,99 € avant remise. Ce robot aspirateur-laveur mise surtout sur son profil de 7,98 cm, sa station d’entretien et une aspiration annoncée à 25 000 Pa.
Le Qrevo Edge 2 vise les foyers qui veulent automatiser à la fois l’aspiration, le lavage et une bonne partie de l’entretien courant. L’offre Amazon à 589,98 € représente une baisse de 300,01 €, soit environ 34 % par rapport au prix de référence indiqué.
Son format très bas lui permet de passer sous davantage de meubles que de nombreux robots à tourelle fixe, tandis que sa station lave les serpillières avec une eau pouvant atteindre 80 °C. Cette offre French Days intéresse donc surtout les logements où les poils, les zones difficiles d’accès et l’entretien des sols reviennent souvent.
Pendant les French Days, le Roborock Qrevo Edge 2 est affiché à 589,98 € au lieu de 889,99 € chez Amazon.
Pourquoi choisir le Roborock Qrevo Edge 2 ?
- Un format plus bas : Avec 7,98 cm de hauteur et un LiDAR rétractable, le robot peut accéder à des espaces où un modèle plus haut risque de rester bloqué devant le meuble.
- Une station très automatisée : La base gère le vidage de la poussière, le lavage des serpillières à l’eau chaude jusqu’à 80 °C et leur séchage à l’air chaud à 55 °C, ce qui réduit les manipulations après chaque cycle.
- Des brosses pensées pour les cheveux : Le système DuoDivide et la brosse latérale FlexiArm sont conçus pour limiter les enchevêtrements et mieux récupérer les cheveux ou poils le long des murs et dans les angles.
Un robot surtout pertinent dans les logements chargés et difficiles d’accès
Le Qrevo Edge 2 combine une aspiration annoncée à 25 000 Pa avec deux serpillières rotatives, dont l’une peut se déporter vers les bords grâce au système FlexiArm. Sa hauteur de 7,98 cm devient particulièrement utile si vous avez des canapés, buffets ou lits avec peu de garde au sol, car le LiDAR se rétracte lorsque le robot doit passer sous un meuble bas. Pour replacer ce modèle face aux autres références, notre comparatif des meilleurs aspirateurs robots en 2026 détaille chez Clubic les critères de navigation, lavage, franchissement et entretien. Ce positionnement conviendra davantage à un foyer avec animaux, cheveux longs ou plusieurs pièces à entretenir qu’à un petit appartement où une station imposante et ce niveau d’automatisation seraient surdimensionnés.
Une fiche technique ambitieuse, mais l’évitement d’obstacles reste à relativiser
Roborock annonce la reconnaissance de plus de 280 types d’objets, mais un essai indépendant récent de Vacuum Wars a mesuré une performance d’évitement inférieure à la moyenne de son protocole, ce qui invite à ne pas laisser traîner câbles et petits objets sans précaution. Le même test a en revanche relevé de très bons résultats sur le nettoyage des tapis, la gestion des cheveux et le lavage, avec pour contreparties un bac à poussière embarqué assez petit et une endurance légèrement en retrait face au premier Qrevo Edge.
✅ Les points forts
- Profil de 7,98 cm avec LiDAR rétractable pour mieux passer sous certains meubles.
- Aspiration annoncée à 25 000 Pa et double système anti-enchevêtrements.
- Serpillière et brosse latérale FlexiArm pour mieux couvrir les bords et les coins.
- Station avec lavage des serpillières jusqu’à 80 °C, séchage à 55 °C et vidage automatique.
- Prix French Days de 589,98 €, soit environ 34 % de baisse par rapport à 889,99 €.
❌ Les limites
- L’évitement d’obstacles n’a pas été irréprochable lors d’un test indépendant récent.
- Le bac à poussière du robot reste compact, même si la station assure le vidage automatique.
- La station occupe nettement plus de place qu’une simple base de recharge.
Si son profil bas et sa station tout-en-un correspondent à votre logement, Amazon propose actuellement le Roborock Qrevo Edge 2 à 589,98 €.
À 589,98 €, le Qrevo Edge 2 devient plus facile à envisager pour qui cherche un robot aspirateur-laveur très autonome sans monter vers les références les plus chères de la marque. Son intérêt tient moins au seul chiffre de 25 000 Pa qu’à l’ensemble formé par le format bas, les éléments FlexiArm, le système anti-enchevêtrements et la station capable de laver puis sécher les serpillières.
Il reste toutefois préférable de garder un sol relativement dégagé, car la reconnaissance d’objets annoncée ne garantit pas un évitement parfait en conditions réelles. Pour un studio ou un logement peu encombré, un modèle moins coûteux et plus simple peut suffire ; pour une maison avec animaux, cheveux longs, meubles bas et plusieurs pièces, cette remise French Days rend le Qrevo Edge 2 nettement plus cohérent.
French Days 2026 : rendez-vous sur Clubic pour les meilleures offres
Au programme : des sélections thématiques, des articles dédiés aux grosses promos à ne pas louper et un suivi en temps réel des deals les plus intéressants chez Amazon, Cdiscount, Fnac, Darty, Boulanger et bien d'’autres.
